SOURCE-BACKED PASSAGE

From the guide

Asked: Why can the 3 Hz samples show a 1 Hz alias?

An ambiguous low-rate trace
At 3 Hz, four samples cover 0 through 1 second. For the 2 Hz reference, a signed −1 Hz alias fits those same samples: its apparent frequency is 1 Hz. Matching the sample points does not identify the original waveform. Record the sampling rate and reference revision with your claim.

Asked: Can these illustrations establish detection accuracy?

Describe what the source supports
These E06 images are prepared illustrations, not camera captures or measured detector outputs. You can describe visible shadows, highlights and edge differences. They cannot establish detection confidence, accuracy or current camera health. A claim about a real detector needs measured outputs and a documented method.

From the guide

Asked: Does interrupted verification remove the restriction?

Repair is not release
Recording a repair does not prove verification. An interrupted verification leaves the restriction in place; release follows a recorded successful verification by the responsible workflow. The assistant cannot repair, verify, release equipment or make bookings. Contact responsible staff for an actual equipment decision.

checks.manual:
READABLE WITHOUT AI

Evidence & equipment decisions

WORKFLOW · revision 01 · Bundled offline copy · publication status unchecked

Keep the claim yours

Write your own notebook claim and connect it to recorded evidence, settings and source revisions. A local draft is not a saved claim, and a saved claim is not a submission receipt. This assistant reads the selected public guide and your question; it cannot inspect browser evidence, verify your submission or author a notebook entry for you.

Section WORKFLOW-notebook
Restriction and occupancy differ

A fault report alone does not impose a restriction. In the demonstrator, classification and a recorded restriction determine the affected component and kit. A restricted required camera makes its complete capture kit unavailable, while unrelated signal equipment stays available. Availability and current occupancy are separate states; this guide does not provide current booking or equipment status.

Section WORKFLOW-restrict
Repair is not release

Recording a repair does not prove verification. An interrupted verification leaves the restriction in place; release follows a recorded successful verification by the responsible workflow. The assistant cannot repair, verify, release equipment or make bookings. Contact responsible staff for an actual equipment decision.

From the guide

Asked: What changes when the field of view widens?

Field of view changes framing
The geometry rehearsal compares fields of view of 18°, 40° and 90° with the camera and objects fixed. A wider field includes more of the conceptual scene while each object occupies less of the frame. This is a teaching model, not a surveyed installation or a calibration of a real lens.
